extracted.intended_audience: SNSF grant applicants and reviewers (Swiss research funding community)
extracted.subtask_description: Official SNSF evaluation procedure describing criteria, process steps, rating scale, and scheme-specific emphases used to assess grant proposals submitted to the Swiss National Science Foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Criteria (top-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess proposals based on criteria defined by the SNSF, which include: scientific relevance of the project; originality of the project; applicant's expertise and scientific track record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three items are the high-level aspects reviewers are explicitly asked to consider when forming assessments of proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on scientific quality over publication metrics (DORA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SNSF promotes the view that scientific quality across a researcher's entire output is much more important than publication metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SNSF does NOT rely on: Journal-based metrics, Journal reputation (impact factor), H-index, Other simplistic metrics. (SNSF is a DORA signatory.) Reviewers should therefore evaluate quality of output and contributions rather than relying on simplistic bibliometric indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection Process Structure — External Review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For most funding schemes, at least two external reviewers assess proposals first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External reviewers are selected for relevant expertise. This step provides independent expert assessments that feed into internal evaluation and panel discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection Process Structure — Internal Review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application is independently evaluated by at least two members of the evaluation panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal reviewers produce recommendations that provide the basis for subsequent panel discussion. Independence of evaluations is emphasised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection Process Structure — Panel Discussion and Consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion by the relevant evaluation panel to build consensus and produce a final ranking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel members discuss applications based on external and internal reviews; consensus-building during the panel meeting determines relative ranking used for funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating scale (1–9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers and panel members rate applications on a uniform scale of 1 to 9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale anchors: 1 = an application has few or no merits and many serious weaknesses; 9 = projects are outstanding in all respects. The procedure notes that thresholds typically require high scores given the competitive landscape. Use the full 1–9 scale when assessing overall merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding decision rule — funding line
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the ranking of proposals and available funding, the National Research Council determines the 'funding line.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals with a score above the funding line will receive funding. Final funding allocation depends on ranking relative to available budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard sub-criteria for Project funding
rubrics_metrics.description: For Project funding (most common scheme) reviewers consider: (1) Scientific quality and originality; (2) Suitability of methods; (3) Scientific significance; (4) Topicality and impact; (5) Feasibility; (6) Quality of the proposal applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sub-criteria should be used to structure assessment of project proposals. Each sub-criterion addresses a distinct dimension of proposal merit: conceptual novelty and rigor, methodological appropriateness, importance to the field, relevance and potential impact, realistic planning and resources, and the applicant's capacity to carry out the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career funding scheme emphases
rubrics_metrics.description: Career-oriented schemes (Ambizione, Eccellenza, etc.) emphasize demonstrated independence, personal achievements, research vision, mobility and broadening of experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating applications to career schemes, reviewers should give particular weight to evidence of the applicant's independence from supervisors, individual accomplishments, clarity and ambition of their research vision, and indications that mobility/broadening experiences strengthen the candidate's development.
